# Contributing to ugroempi/CAs

First off, thanks for taking the time to contribute! Contributions are encouraged and valued. 

See the [Table of Contents](#table-of-contents) for different ways to help. Please make sure to read the relevant section before making your contribution. It will make it a lot easier for me and smooth out the experience for you.

## I Want To Contribute

### Legal Notice 
> When contributing to this project, you must agree that you have authored 100% of the content, that you have the necessary rights to the content and that the content you contribute may be provided under the project license.

### General Rules
Contributions must be R only, as the package **CAs** will not switch to including other languages. If you have useful contributions e.g. in C++, you could always provide a package of your own that can be used from within R (as, e.g., the package **caverify** by [@chrispbsmolen](https://github.com/chrispbsmolen)).

Contributors must identify themselves as a living person and must make transparent inhowfar AI was involved in creating the contribution. Contributors are personally (as opposed to legally) responsible for the correctness of the contribution. That responsibility cannot be deferred to an AI.

It is perfectly acceptable to reach out via my university email if that feels more comfortable than opening an issue on GitHub. Exception: Bugs should always be reported on GitHub so that others can see that they have been noted.

### Reporting Bugs or Making Suggestions
Bug reports on package behavior and documentation are always welcome. Other suggestions or requests for enhancements are also welcome but will be treated with less urgency.

I use GitHub issues to track bugs, errors or other wishes and suggestions. In any such case:

- Open an issue. 
- Explain the behavior you would expect or wish for and the actual behavior.
- Make sure that you use the latest package version.
- Please provide as much context as possible and describe the *reproduction steps* that someone else can follow to recreate the issue on their own. This usually includes your code. For good bug reports you should isolate the problem and create a reduced test case.

### Improvements on Covering Array Numbers
I provide a frozen status of Charles Colbourn's covering array tables at [https://github.com/ugroempi/CAs/blob/main/ColbournTables.md](https://github.com/ugroempi/CAs/blob/main/ColbournTables.md). I do not update or maintain them. If you (believe to) have found a smaller covering array than listed in these tables, this will only be of interest for me in exceptional cases and for very small arrays. You can report such arrays to [@chrispbsmolen](https://github.com/chrispbsmolen) for his repository `ca-tools`.

### Pull Requests
If you think that you have a contribution to make, one way of doing so may be a pull request (PR). Typically, a pull request should be initiated via an issue. The discussion following that issue may then lead to in invitation to submit a PR.

## Attribution for your contribution
Make sure to credit all relevant sources in your contribution. 

In particular, especially with mathematical content, make sure to be transparent about the involvement of AI, and 
whether **you as a human fully understand and take responsibility for your entire contribution** (expected, unless you explicitly say otherwise) or rely on the correctness of an AI-driven proof.

If you contribute code to the package **CAs**, you will be credited as a contributor to the package.

## Attribution for this guide
This guide is is a heavily-edited version of the **contributing.md** [example](https://contributing.md/) at https://contributing.md/example/.
